training-instructors.purpose: Instructor and SME qualification pipeline: nominations, observed deliveries, qualification and annual currency.

team-ojt.title: Team practice readiness

competencies-levels.title: How levels work
competencies-levels.purpose: The four Kafa'a levels with generic attributes across every skill, the "not yet" state, Authority above Expert, and why skills exist only at some levels.

competencies-descriptors.title: Level descriptor library
competencies-descriptors.purpose: Every skill with the levels where it exists, its track and behaviourally anchored indicators, searchable in English and Arabic.

competencies-descriptor.title: Level descriptors
competencies-descriptor.purpose: A skill's observable indicators at each level, the rationale for its range, generic attributes and external equivalents.

competencies-scale.title: Level map
competencies-scale.purpose: The Kafa'a scale mapped to SFIA, SkillsFuture, DigComp, UNESCO and the UAE NQF, with the fit and a source on every row.

my-levels.title: My levels explained
my-levels.purpose: What I am seen to do at my level, what to show next, what my levels read as elsewhere, and my Authority recognitions.

admin-descriptors.title: Level descriptors editor
admin-descriptors.purpose: Write and publish descriptors and level ranges; coverage against the descriptor rules; auditors read.

admin-authority.title: Authority recognitions
admin-authority.purpose: Propose Experts for Authority with a panel; the HR director decides as a second approver; never a fifth level.

masked: Shown as qualified / not qualified only
securityMasked: Security qualification: Kafa'a mirrors qualified or not qualified only. Tasks, dates and evaluators stay in ENEC's security systems.
requalNote: Requalification every {n} months. Notices go out 90, 60 and 30 days before expiry unless the standard sets other intervals.

mirror.title: A mirror, not the record
mirror.body: Until ENEC approves Kafa'a as the system of record, these cards mirror ENEC's training records system. Kafa'a never sets a qualification status by itself: changes come from evaluations signed by a qualified evaluator, or from the source system.

eval.title: Task evaluation
eval.criticalHint: A failed critical step fails the task whatever else went well.
eval.criticalNote: This is a critical task: a failed critical step fails the evaluation.
eval.correctHint: Records are append-only: a correction adds a new entry that supersedes the earlier one.
eval.confirmBody: You are recording {result} on {task} for {person}. This cannot be edited later; a correction would be a new entry.
eval.selfBody: An evaluator cannot sign off their own qualification. The request will be refused and logged.
eval.notEvaluatorTitle: You do not hold the evaluator qualification for this standard
eval.notEvaluatorBody: You can view records, but sign-offs will be refused until your evaluator qualification for this standard is current.

gap.none: No required standards recorded for this role

lib.intro: What "competent" means for nuclear roles at Barakah: 14 domains, four levels, and the roles that need each competency.
lib.layer1Body: Proficiency levels describe how far someone has developed in a domain. They guide development plans and career moves. They do not authorise anyone to do safety-related work.
lib.layer2Body: Qualification cards record who is qualified to do which task, with an evaluator's sign-off and an expiry. This is what authorises work. Staff see their own cards under My qualifications.
lib.satTitle: Built on the Systematic Approach to Training
lib.satBody: Job and task analysis produces task lists; task lists produce qualification cards; cards are completed through on-the-job training and task performance evaluations, including job performance measures (JPMs).
lib.compsDesc: {n} competencies in {d} domains. Open one for its level descriptors and the roles that need it.
lib.heatTitle: Highest level required, by domain and job family
lib.heatDesc: Each cell shows the highest proficiency level any role in the family needs in the domain (empty = not required).

verify.intro: Check a Kafa'a-issued course certificate by its number. Only internal courses issue these certificates.
verify.notFanrTitle: This is not an operator licence check
verify.notFanrBody: Kafa'a never verifies FANR operator certificates. Operator certification is recorded by FANR.
verify.note: Internal Kafa'a course certificate. Not an operator licence.
verify.notFoundBody: We could not find {no}. Check the number on the certificate and try again.
verify.format: Use letters, digits and hyphens only (6 to 32 characters).

my.intro: Your qualification cards, task by task: status, evaluator role, date and expiry.
my.noneBody: Cards appear here when you start a qualification standard for your role.
my.gapTarget: Standards for a role I want
my.pickTarget: Choose a role to see which of its qualification standards you already hold.
my.openPlanner: Plan the path to this role

team.intro: Qualification readiness for the people in your scope, with expiries, acknowledgements and notices.
team.noTeam: No one in your scope yet
team.noTeamBody: Your scope is set by your role assignment (for example a crew or a team).
team.noticesBody: Notices go to each person and their manager 90, 60 and 30 days before a qualification expires (or at the standard's own intervals). Items within 30 days show as due in the matrix.
team.sweepConsequence: Kafa'a checks every record in your scope, sends any notices not already sent, marks records due within 30 days, and marks past-dated records expired.
team.calendarDesc: Qualifications expiring in the next {n} days.
team.acksDesc: Sign-off flow: trainee, qualified evaluator, then supervisor acknowledgement.
team.ackConsequence: You confirm, as supervisor, the evaluation of {task} for {person}. You cannot acknowledge an evaluation you performed.

crew.title: Crew licences
crew.desc: Certificate validity and this quarter's shift proficiency for your crew.
crew.note: Shift supervisors see validity and proficiency for their crew only, and availability as available or not available. No medical detail is shown.
crew.none: No licensed operators in your scope

matrix.intro: People in your scope against qualification standards, coloured by status. Due means within 30 days of expiry.
matrix.tabWho: Who is qualified for task X
matrix.footnote: * needs review after a standard revision. Security qualifications show qualified or not qualified only. Select a person for their cards and gap analysis.

who.desc: For work planners: people in your scope who currently hold the qualification and have passed the task.
who.none: No one in your scope is qualified for this task
who.noneBody: Check another task, or ask the training team about upcoming evaluations.
who.scopeNote: Limited to people in your scope

stds.intro: Qualification standards (versioned qualification cards) with task lists, JPMs, requalification intervals and the records that depend on them.
stds.title: Title
stds.noEvaluator: You do not hold an evaluator qualification.
stds.queueEmpty: Nothing waiting on standards you evaluate.

std.revisedBody: {n} records were flagged for review. Decide each one in the review tab: carry it over or require retraining.
std.restrictedBody: Security training content stays in ENEC's security systems. Kafa'a shows qualified or not qualified only.
std.satBody: Trainee completes on-the-job training; a qualified evaluator signs each task (JPMs where listed); the supervisor acknowledges. Records are append-only: corrections create a new entry with a reason.
std.noRecordsBody: Records appear for people in your scope who hold or are working on this standard.
std.recordOnOtherVersion: This record is on version {v}. Review it to move it to the current version before evaluating.
std.noReviewBody: Records are flagged here when a revision changes this standard.
std.reviewBody: A change to the task list or procedure may affect these people. Carry a record over when the change does not affect them, or require retraining.
std.reviewConsequence: The record moves to the current version of the standard. Retraining sets it to in progress until the changed tasks are evaluated again.
std.impactBody: {n} records on this version will be flagged for review.
std.reasonHint: For example: procedure revision after a modification or an operating-experience lesson.
std.taskEdits: Task list for the new version

reasons.ins_fit: Has {have} of the {need} skills this standard covers at level 2 or above
reasons.ins_sme_profile: Has a subject-matter expert profile in the knowledge capture studio
reasons.ojt_no_ready: No preceptor has marked this task ready yet
reasons.ojt_not_signoff: Practice is not a sign-off: only an evaluator's sign-off changes the qualification

ins.localisationLink: Localisation countdown to 2030: when UAE instructors take over each partner-delivered programme (readiness computed from this pipeline)
ins.mirrorBody: Kafa'a mirrors the licensee's instructor qualification records to plan the pipeline. It issues no FANR status: qualification decisions stay with the licensee's training organisation. The currency rule (40 delivery hours and 8 hours of continuing development a year) is a SAMPLE demo setting.

currency.title: Annual currency
currency.lapsedOn: Currency lapsed on {date}: the 12-month window ended under the minimum.
currency.rule: Currency lapses when the hours in a 12-month window fall below the minimum; notices go out 90, 60 and 30 days before the review date.

req.accepted: Nomination accepted by the training manager
req.initialWait: Assigned on acceptance; completion comes from the training records system
req.coTeach: Two co-teach observations passed, by two different observers
req.solo: One solo observed delivery passed, by a third observer
req.qualifiedWait: The training manager confirms; an observer of the set cannot

form.title: Record an observation
form.rule: Pass needs 75% or more and no critical item rated "not met". You cannot observe yourself; qualification needs three different observers.
form.confirmBody: {kind}: {score}%, {result}. Observations are append-only; a correction is a new observation.

hours.logBody: Records delivery or development hours for this instructor (mirror of the scheduling system).
hours.logBodySelf: Records your own continuing development hours.

nominate.title: Nominate {name} for the instructor track
nominate.body: The training manager decides the nomination. On acceptance the instructor initial training course is assigned.
nominate.motivation: Why this person (or you) should teach
nominate.securityNote: Security standards and security, cyber and safeguards roles are career-path only and never join the track.

facts.title: Programme facts
facts.asipBody: Barakah foundation training includes the Accelerated SRO Instructor Program and the Instructor Initial and Continuing Training Qualification (per source).
facts.asipSrc: UAE National Report, 10th CNS Review Meeting (March 2026), Art. 11, p. 75
facts.reg16Body: FANR-REG-16 Art. 9 requires systematic, performance-based training delivered by qualified instructors, including for contractors.
facts.fanr65Body: FANR's own Internal Trainer Qualification Programme certifies 65 subject-matter experts to deliver technical and non-technical training (the regulator's programme, per source).
facts.fanr65Src: UAE National Report, 10th CNS Review Meeting (March 2026), Art. 8, p. 40

board.intro: The pool of qualified instructors with their annual currency, the pipeline from SME nomination to qualification, the observation queue and the teaching hours log.
board.statPipelineSub: {ready} ready to qualify · {nominated} nominations to decide
board.statHours: Delivery hours in the current windows
board.sweepBody: Instructors whose 12-month window ended under the minimum lapse on that date and their evaluator rows end; the others are renewed; 90, 60 and 30-day notices go to instructors short of hours.
board.syncBody: Delivered M04 sessions with at least one attendee marked present are added once to the instructor's hours log.
board.poolCaption: Qualified instructors and their annual currency
board.queueEmpty: No candidate is waiting for an observation
board.queueIntro: Candidates waiting for a co-teach or solo observation. You cannot observe your own track; the qualifying set needs three different observers.

act.youObserved: You observed this candidate: another training manager may need to qualify them
act.acceptBody: The instructor initial training course is assigned and the candidate is told to start.
act.declineBody: The candidate sees your reason and can volunteer again later.
act.qualifyBody: Records the qualification (maker-checker), starts the annual currency, writes evaluator rows for the standards and adds the instructing skill to the person's skills profile.
act.reinstateBody: A passed currency observation after the lapse restarts the annual currency and the evaluator rows.
act.withdrawBody: The track closes; a qualified instructor's evaluator rows end today.

find.none: No colleague in your view matches this standard yet

track.notFound: This instructor track is not in your view
track.intro: Stages, observed deliveries, annual currency and teaching hours for one instructor.
track.ownNote: This is your own track: you cannot observe or qualify yourself.
track.makerBody: You observed part of this candidate's qualifying set, and no complete set exists without you. Another training manager has to decide.
track.observationsIntro: Checklist of observable behaviours tied to the course objectives (the F25 level-3 mechanics). Critical items must not be "not met".
track.evaluatorNone: None yet: they are written when the instructor qualifies
track.evaluatorNote: Written by the qualification and kept in step with the currency; they end when the currency lapses or the track closes.

my.intro: Teach what you know: from SME nomination to qualified instructor, with your observed deliveries and annual currency in one place.

next.nominated: The training manager is reviewing your nomination.
next.initial_training: Complete the instructor initial training course ({code}). It is in My learning.
next.co_teach: Co-teach two sessions with two different instructors observing you.
next.solo: Deliver one session on your own, observed by a third instructor.
next.ready: All observations are complete: the training manager will confirm your qualification.
next.lapsed: Your currency lapsed. A passed currency observation lets the training manager reinstate you.
next.currencyShort: Before {date} you still need {hours} delivery hours and {cpd} development hours.
next.currencyOk: Your currency for this year is met. Keep teaching and logging your development.

my.how1: Volunteer, or be nominated by your line manager or the training manager.
my.how2: The training manager accepts and assigns {code}.
my.how3: Co-teach twice, observed by two different instructors.
my.how4: Deliver solo, observed by a third instructor.
my.how5: The training manager qualifies you; keep 40 delivery and 8 development hours a year.
my.withdrawBody: Your track closes. You can volunteer again later.
my.teachBody: Your skills profile suggests standards you could teach. Volunteer and the training manager will review it.
my.notStaff: The instructor track is open to ENEC staff.
my.noMatch: No standard matches your skills profile at level 2 yet. You can still volunteer.

team.intro: Find subject-matter experts in your team and nominate them; follow their progress on the instructor track.
team.tracks: My team on the instructor track
team.tracksIntro: Tracks of people in your scope.
team.noTracks: Nobody in your team is on the instructor track yet
team.findIntro: Ranked from the skills profile, SME profiles and SME mentor nominations. No personal attributes are used.
team.how: Your nomination goes to the training manager. Accepted candidates take the instructor initial training, co-teach twice and deliver solo before they qualify.

ojt.intro: Record each practice of a qualification task with the preceptor who watched you. When you have enough supervised performances and your preceptor says you are ready, ask an evaluator to sign the task off.
ojt.notice: Logbook entries and preceptor acknowledgements are practice records. They never change your qualification status: only an evaluator's sign-off in the qualification record does.

modeHint.walkthrough: talked through the steps with the preceptor
modeHint.simulate: practised on the simulator or a mock-up

ojt.dateHint: Up to 180 days back, never in the future.
ojt.noPreceptor: No qualified preceptor for this task
ojt.preceptorHint: Someone qualified on this standard, not yourself.
ojt.whereHint: For example: Unit 2 turbine hall, night shift.
ojt.noteHint: What went well, what to work on (up to 500 characters).
ojt.requestBody: The evaluator receives your practice record and readiness. Their sign-off goes into your qualification record as usual.
ojt.noEvaluator: No evaluator available for this task
ojt.noRecord: You need a qualification record for this standard first.
ojt.cancelBody: The evaluator is told the request was withdrawn. Your practice entries stay.
ojt.feedbackHint: At least 3 characters. The trainee sees this.
ojt.noTasksBody: Practice tasks appear here when you have a qualification standard in progress or required by your role.
ojt.offlineBody: You can keep logging practice. Entries stay on this device and are sent once when you are back online.
ojt.synced: Synced {n}, already recorded {d}, refused {f}, still waiting {k}.
ojt.ackIntro: Entries that name you as preceptor. Acknowledging is feedback on practice; it is not a sign-off.
ojt.ackEmptyBody: Entries that name you as preceptor appear here.
ojt.ackNotSignoff: Practice, not a sign-off: your acknowledgement does not change the person's qualification.
ojt.readyHint: Tick when you would be comfortable with an evaluator assessing this task now.
ojt.evalIntro: Requests that name you as evaluator. Sign the task off in the qualification record; the request closes with it.
ojt.evalEmptyBody: Requests that name you as evaluator appear here.
ojt.signoffBody: This is the qualification sign-off: it is recorded as an evaluation on the person's qualification record.
ojt.declineBody: The person is told you declined, with your reason.

team.intro: Practice and readiness for the people in your scope. Read only: acknowledgements stay with the named preceptor and sign-offs with the evaluator.
team.readySub: Enough supervised practice and a ready
team.caption: Practice readiness by person and task
team.emptyBody: When people in your scope log practice, their readiness appears here.

ci.notDefined: This skill is not defined at this level.

lv.intro: Kafa'a uses four levels. Each one means the same thing across every skill, through five generic attributes, and each skill describes what someone at a level is seen to do.
lv.tSkillsSub: of {n} skills, at every level where they exist
lv.tLevelsSub: a descriptor per skill and level
lv.scaleDesc: From "not yet" to Expert, with Authority above it as a recognition, not a level.
lv.notYetBody: Not held yet, or not assessed yet. Kafa'a shows "not yet", never a zero.
lv.authorityBody: Recognised by a panel for setting the standard beyond ENEC. Never a fifth level, never gamified.
lv.sfiaHint: The SFIA 9 level of responsibility this level corresponds to
lv.attrsDesc: SFIA-style attributes that make a level mean the same thing in operations, maintenance or quality.
lv.rangesTitle: Why a skill is not defined at every level
lv.rangesDesc: Like SFIA, a skill is described only at the levels where it really exists. Every range has a published rationale.
lv.trackDesc: Behavioural skills use the same evidence model as technical skills (IAEA-TECDOC-1917).
lv.trackCallout: One evidence model for every skill
lv.trackBody: {n} behavioural skills (human performance, leadership, safety culture and the transversal skills) are described with observable indicators and assessed by observation, simulator debriefs, situational judgement and peer input, never by self-description alone.

basisBody.full: Held from first awareness to setting the standard for others.
basisBody.licence_like: A qualified plant task is done under supervision or not at all; awareness of it sits with the parent skill.
basisBody.leading: Leading, coaching or instructing begins when you do it for someone; awareness is covered by human performance skills.
basisBody.not_operated: Advanced-reactor skills stop at Qualified: Expert needs an operating plant to set the standard on. No deployment decision implied.
basisBody.awareness_only: All-staff cyber and security hygiene is awareness content; deeper levels belong to security roles at career-path level only.
basisBody.watch: A watch horizon with no plant to operate, so independent and expert levels are not defined.
basisBody.declining: A declining or obsolete practice: descriptors stay so past assessments remain readable, with no Expert level.

modeHint.observation: Seen doing it on the job by a qualified observer.
modeHint.simulator: Seen in a simulator scenario and discussed in the debrief.
modeHint.jpm: A job performance measure performed to standard.
modeHint.records: Logs, sheets and records show it was done right.
modeHint.work_product: A document, analysis or package that shows the level.
modeHint.interview: Explains the why behind the work in a structured interview.
modeHint.peer: Colleagues who work alongside describe what they see.
modeHint.sjt: Chooses well in realistic situational judgement items.
modeHint.attestation: A supervisor attests to what was seen over time.

why.none: No level range is published for this skill yet.
why.range: {skill} is defined from level {from} to level {to}.
why.sfia: SFIA 9 defines each skill only at the levels where it exists, and publishes why.

basis.full: Held from first awareness to setting the standard.
basis.licence_like: Qualified plant tasks are done under supervision or not at all.
basis.leading: Leading starts when you lead someone.
basis.not_operated: Expert needs an operating plant; no deployment decision implied.
basis.awareness_only: All-staff hygiene is awareness; security roles stay at career-path level.
basis.watch: A watch horizon: nothing to operate yet.
basis.declining: A practice being retired keeps its history but no Expert level.

dl.intro: Every skill described at the levels where it exists, with a level essence and observable indicators in English and Arabic. Search indicator text in either language.

dp.intro: What someone at each level is seen to do, with the evidence an assessor uses. Levels outside the skill's range say why.
dp.youHold: You hold this skill at level {level} · {name}
dp.youNotYet: You do not hold this skill yet
dp.youNotYetBody: Level 1 below shows what to start with.
dp.ladderDesc: Indicators describe what is observed, not what someone says about themself.
dp.authorityBody: Above Expert, a panel can recognise someone as an Authority on this skill. It is a recognition, never a fifth level, and it does not change the skill level.
dp.toScale: How Kafa'a maps to other scales
dp.crosswalkDesc: How this skill's levels line up with the frameworks it is aligned to (FS08 crosswalk).
dp.noCrosswalk: No published alignment for this skill.

sc.intro: How the Kafa'a scale reads in SFIA 9, SkillsFuture, DigComp, UNESCO's AI competency framework and the UAE National Qualifications Framework. Each row cites its source; loose fits say why.
sc.howBody: Kafa'a has four levels plus "not yet". Other frameworks have three to ten. Exact and close fits can be used to compare people and roles; loose fits are indicative only.
sc.gridDesc: External level range, label and fit for each band.

why.fit: A fit is close when the level descriptions match in autonomy and complexity, loose when the frameworks measure different things.
why.source: Every row cites the framework's own source and the date it was read.
why.authority: Authority sits above Expert as a recognition; in other frameworks it reads loosely as their top levels.

sc.stripsDesc: Each external level coloured by the Kafa'a band it maps to.
sc.stripAria: {fw} levels and the Kafa'a bands they map to
sc.followN: {n} of {total} crosswalk rows follow this map
sc.authDesc: Something above Expert, without inventing a fifth level.
sc.auth1Body: Proposed by the training manager with a panel (HR authority, skill owner, an external peer) and a citation, then decided by the HR director, who is never the proposer. Every recognition writes a ledger record.
sc.auth2Body: The skill level stays Expert. Authority is not scored, ranked or counted in readiness, and it earns no points or badges.
sc.auth3Body: The panel decides "recognised" (reviewed every three years) or "not yet", with a note on what would make the difference.
sc.mirrorBody: The NQF column is indicative until NQC-recognised assessors review it. Kafa'a is not a recognition or licensing authority, and nothing here awards a qualification.

ml.intro: Each skill you hold, described by what you are seen to do at your level and what to show next. External equivalents are indicative.
ml.empty: No skills on your passport yet.
ml.authDesc: A recognition above Expert, decided by a panel and the HR director.
ml.levelStays: Your skill level stays Expert: Authority is not a level.
ml.neverBody: No points, badges or rankings come with Authority, and it never changes your skill level or readiness.
ml.noDescriptor: No descriptor published at this level yet.
ml.topExpert: You are at Expert, the top level. Above it, a panel can recognise you as an Authority.
ml.topRange: This is the highest level defined for this skill.

why.expert: Expert is the top level of the Kafa'a scale; Authority is a recognition, not a level.
why.range: The skill's published range ends here.

da.intro: Descriptors and level ranges for every skill. Levels inside a range are always published; levels outside it are drafts until the range is extended. Nothing is deleted.
da.readOnlyBody: You can read every descriptor, including drafts and archived ones. Editing is for framework owners.
da.tMissingSub: levels missing or outside a range
da.tableDesc: Open a skill to edit its descriptors and range.
da.inRange: Inside the range: saved as published.
da.outRange: Outside the range: saved as a draft.
da.willDraft: Saving keeps it as a draft.
da.confirmPublish: The descriptor is published at once and replaces the current text. The change is audited.
da.confirmDraft: The descriptor is saved as a draft (not public). The change is audited.
da.rangeHint: Every level in the range needs a descriptor (draft or published). Extending publishes the drafts; shrinking archives published levels outside the range.
da.confirmRange: Descriptors inside the range are published and published ones outside it are archived. The change is audited.

msg.obsolete: This skill is obsolete: its descriptors stay readable but are no longer edited.
msg.restricted: Security and cyber-hygiene skills stay at awareness levels (1-2); deeper levels belong to security roles at career-path level only.
msg.essence: Give a level essence in English and Arabic (up to 200 characters each).
msg.count: Give 2 to 4 observable indicators in each language.
msg.mismatch: Give the same number of indicators in English and Arabic.
msg.indicator: Each indicator is a non-empty sentence of up to 220 characters.
msg.duplicate: Each indicator must say something different.
msg.template: This reuses the old template sentence: describe what someone at this level is seen to do.
msg.in_range: This level is inside the skill's range: its descriptor is always published.
msg.out_of_range: This level is outside the skill's range: save it as a draft, then extend the range.
msg.range: Choose a range from level 1 to 4, lowest first.
msg.basis: Choose why the skill exists at these levels.
msg.rationale: Give the rationale in English and Arabic (20 to 400 characters each).
msg.incomplete: Write a descriptor for every level in the new range first.

au.intro: Authority recognises an Expert who sets the standard beyond ENEC. A panel proposes it; the HR director decides as a second approver.
au.neverBody: Authority never becomes a fifth level, never changes a skill level or readiness, and carries no points, badges or rankings.
au.tExpertsSub: level 4 on a skill that can be recognised
au.queueDesc: The HR director decides; the proposer cannot.
au.makerChecker: You proposed this: another approver (the HR director) must decide it.
au.candDesc: People at Expert (level 4) on a skill that can be recognised. Security and cyber-hygiene skills are excluded.

why.expert: Holds the skill at Expert ({basis} evidence).
why.panel: A panel and a second approver decide; the proposer never does.
why.level: The skill level stays 4 whatever the outcome.

dlgBody.approve: {name} will be recognised as an Authority on {skill}. A ledger record is written and a review is set for three years. The skill level stays Expert.
dlgBody.not_yet: {name} will not be recognised on {skill} for now. Your note tells them what would make the difference.
dlgBody.withdraw: The recognition of {name} on {skill} ends. A current recognition writes a ledger record.

au.eligibleBody: Holds the skill at Expert ({basis}, confidence {conf}).
au.proposeOk: The proposal can be sent to the HR director.
au.proposeConsequence: The HR director is notified and decides. You will not be able to decide it yourself. The proposal is audited.

msg.person: Choose an active member of staff.
msg.restricted: Security and cyber-hygiene skills are not recognised individually.
msg.not_expert: Only Experts (level 4) can be recognised; Authority is never a fifth level.
msg.conflict: There is already an open or current recognition on this skill.
msg.citation: Write the citation in English and Arabic (20 to 400 characters each).
